newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia SBS-Agro says owned Sibneft tender winner.
newsitem.headline: Russia SBS-Agro says owned Sibneft tender winner.

text.p: One of Russia's biggest banks, SBS-Agro, said on Tuesday it had had control of the mystery winner of a controversial tender on May 12 for 51 percent of oil company Sibneft but declined to say if it still had links to the firm.

Banking sources said on Tuesday that SBS-Agro owned 100 percent of Alkion Securities, which in turn owns 95 percent of Sibneft tender winner OOO Finansovaya Neftyanaya Korporatsiya (Financial Oil Corporation or FNK).
They said SBS-Agro also controls the remaining five percent through Unified Depositary Company, equal portions of which are owned by SBS-Agro and four affiliates.
"We do not deny the fact that there were such founders at the moment when the above companies were created," an SBS-Agro spokesman told Reuters when asked if SBS-Agro owned the two companies.
"However, that does not mean that those companies have the same shareholders now."
FNK won the tender with a bid of $110 million, far short of the likely true value of Sibneft, against a starting price of $101 million.
SBS-Agro handled funds from bidders under the official tender conditions.
Russia's third biggest bank by assets Uneximbank (Oneksimbank in Russian), whose bid was rejected by the tender organisers, has said it will protest against the results in court soon.

The 51 percent Sibneft stake had been held in trust by another little-known oil industry investment vehicle, ZAO Neftyanaya Finansovaya Kompaniya (NFK), which is associated with businessman and presidential security adviser Boris Berezovsky.
Berezovsky, whose company took control of the Sibneft stake in 1995 under the government's shares-for-loans scheme with a credit to the state of 100.3 million, has denied links to FNK.

The shares-for-loans scheme itself, under which investors lent the government money in return for the right to manage state-owned stakes in partly privatised companies, was widely criticised, as stakes often went to the very companies organising the loan tenders for the government.
Uneximbank, which is headed by former First Deputy Prime Minister Vladimir Potanin, has itself been a major beneficiary of this type of privatisation.
Sibirskaya Neftyanaya Kompaniya (Sibneft) is Russia's seventh largest oil group and is chaired by Gazprom chairman Rem Vyakhirev. Its main production unit is Noyabrksneftegaz.
In 1996 ZAO Rifile-Oil won 15 percent of shares and ZAO Sins won 19 percent. The ownership of these two companies has not been published.
Uneximbank owns 85 percent of SIDANKO, Russia's fifth biggest oil group, and a 38 percent stake in metals mining concern Norilsk Nickel.
